trial_court: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Murshidabad in Misc. Case No. 80(iv) of 1988
case_name: Rampada Biswas vs Dolly Mitra And Ors.
facts_of_case: The petitioner's wife filed an application under Section 125, Criminal Procedure Code for maintenance at the rate of Rs. 750/- per month. The trial court granted the relief. The petitioner challenged this order.

legal_principles.principle: A maintenance to the extent of more than the claim of the opposite party No. 1 in her application has been awarded.
legal_principles.held: The Trial Court relied more on surmises and conjectures than on the materials on record.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the applicant to prove that he is unable to maintain himself and his wife.
legal_principles.held: There is no positive finding that there was neglect or refusal by the petitioner to maintain the wife and that the opposite party No. 1 is unable to maintain herself.

legal_principles.principle: A decree in the Matrimonial Suit declaring the marriage as a nullity does not automatically make the opposite party No. 1 a divorcee for the purpose of maintenance under Section 125 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
legal_principles.held: In view of a decree in the Matrimonial Suit preferred by the petitioner against the opposite party No. 1 declaring the marriage as a nullity, whether the opposite party No. 1 can be called a divorcee as to get maintenance under Section 125 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
cited_cases: K. Sivarama Krishna Prasad v. K. Bharathi &Anr., (1996) Cr. LJ 317
Krishna Gopal v. Usha Rani, (1982) Cr. LJ 901

outcome.final_order: The interim maintenance passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate was set aside.
